claim_text: Atlassian opened a Bitbucket status incident at 10:19 AM ET on Nov 23 for failing OAuth token requests
summary: Atlassian's Bitbucket status page opened an incident, 'Authentication service degraded', at 10:19 AM ET (15:19 UTC) on Nov 23. OAuth token requests may fail or time out. It was not resolved at 11:12 AM ET.
detail: The status page lists two updates: Investigating (10:19 AM) and a second at 11:08 AM ET. Times are the status page's own, converted from UTC. Related services may be unavailable or degraded, it says.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Atlassian's own status page and its public incident feed give the incident, its start time and its state.

claim_text: The incident lists Authentication and user management and Pipelines as partial outages; the Bitbucket website, API and Git access show operational
summary: The incident covers two Bitbucket components, Authentication and user management and Pipelines, both partial outage at our last check. The website, API, Git over SSH and HTTPS and webhooks showed operational.
detail: A partial outage is Atlassian's term for part of a service being affected. The summary page at an earlier read listed only Authentication as degraded, so the Pipelines listing may have been added after the first post. Atlassian's main status page, which covers its other products, showed all systems operational.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The component states are read straight from Atlassian's public status feed.

claim_text: Developers who log in through Atlassian sign-in or use Bitbucket Pipelines are the people affected
summary: The status page describes failing OAuth token requests, the sign-in step, and Pipelines is Bitbucket's build tool, so this mostly hits developers. CircleCI posted that its Bitbucket users had failed logins and called it upstream.
detail: Atlassian has not said how many customers or regions are affected, or whether Jira or Confluence share the same sign-in service.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Atlassian describes the failing sign-in service; CircleCI, an independent company, reports failed Bitbucket logins on its own status page.
notes: The CircleCI post is timed 2:51 PM UTC by the aggregator page, a few minutes before Atlassian opened its incident, and the aggregator may show a shifted clock. The press note that reports began at 9:53 AM ET comes from Downdetector, a user-report tracker.

claim_text: Users reported Bitbucket problems before Atlassian posted an incident
summary: An Australian outlet reports that Downdetector flagged Bitbucket problems from 9:53 AM ET, and that the Bitbucket status page still read all systems operational late in the morning. Atlassian opened its incident at 10:19 AM ET.
detail: The outlet's page was written while the status page was still clear; Atlassian's incident page now shows the 10:19 AM start. Downdetector counts user reports, which can spike for local reasons.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet relays a user-report tracker; Atlassian's own timestamp is the later start. We have not seen Downdetector's data directly.

claim_text: Atlassian has said the Bitbucket and sign-in problem was a hack
summary: Atlassian has not said the problem was an attack. Its status page names no cause and does not use the words attack, breach or hack.
detail: The status page says only that Atlassian has 'identified the cause' and is working on a mitigation.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing on the status page or feed points to a security cause, and no source says Atlassian ruled one out either.

claim_text: Anyone has claimed responsibility for the Bitbucket and sign-in outage
summary: We found no claim of responsibility and no report from an outside researcher, authority or news outlet saying the outage was an attack.
detail: Outlets we found describe it only as an outage and describe user reports.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The sources describe a service failure and make no mention of an attacker.

summary: Atlassian says it has identified the cause and is working on a mitigation at 11:08 AM ET. It has not said what the cause is.
detail: The 10:19 AM post said Atlassian was still working to identify a resolution. We found no post-incident report.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The status page's two updates name no cause.

summary: Atlassian gives no number of affected customers or regions.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The status page does not size the impact.

claim_text: Atlassian said at 11:08 AM ET that it had identified the cause and was working on a mitigation
summary: Atlassian's second status update, at 11:08 AM ET (16:08 UTC), says it has identified the cause, teams are working on a mitigation, and affected users may see requests fail or time out.
detail: This confirms what Atlassian said, not an independent finding. The update does not say what the cause is.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The wording is on Atlassian's own incident page and public feed.
